CTGAN produced the highest-fidelity synthetic data and preserved utility for downstream Random Forest classification comparably to real data, while CopulaGAN performed moderately and TableGAN failed outright. SDV's CTGAN and CopulaGAN synthesizers (the latter documented via docs.sdv.dev) are run directly as the generative models under comparison, with CTGAN's output driving the paper's headline results.
evidence: "Three open-source models (CTGAN, TableGAN, and CopulaGAN) were used to generate synthetic data from the Kaloleni/Rabai HDSS dataset"; CopulaGANSynthesizer cited via docs.sdv.dev in references.
needs: Full affiliations for authors beyond the first three (Rego, Weinheimer-Haus, Alarakhiya, Ngugi, Price, Zhu, Wong, Siwo) were not visible in the provided evidence.

title: Synthetic Data Generation for Healthcare: Exploring Generative Adversarial Networks Variants for Medical Tabular Data
summary: This paper evaluates six GAN variants (GAN, CGAN, CTGAN, CramerGAN, DRAGAN, WGAN) for generating synthetic tabular healthcare data across three medical datasets, assessing classification performance with XGBoost and SVM and using statistical tests to identify the best variant per dataset. CTGAN was frequently among the top-ranked models by the Friedman test, outperforming other GANs on several datasets. The authors explicitly state they used the pre-existing CTGAN library for its implementation, running SDV's CTGAN synthesizer as one of several generators evaluated against each other.
evidence: "For CTGAN implementation, we utilised the pre-existing CTGAN [56] library." CTGAN was run directly as one of six GAN variants and was top-ranked by the Friedman test on two of three datasets.
venue: International Journal of Data Science and Analytics

title: Synthetic Data Generation for Medical Data Privacy and Improved Classification Performance
summary: This work generates synthetic tabular data from the MIMIC-III clinical database to address patient-privacy constraints and severe class imbalance in predicting 30-day hospital readmissions, integrating multiple tables and engineering features like length of stay and age at admission. The authors describe CTGAN's mode-specific handling of continuous features and its Gumbel-softmax-based modeling of categorical variables as the mechanism for producing realistic, privacy-preserving samples that improve downstream classification. CTGAN is the generative model used to synthesize the medical training data underpinning the paper's empirical results.
evidence: "This method enables CTGAN to capture complex dependencies and feature interactions within tabular data" and "CTGAN employs Gumbel-softmax activation to model categorical features effectively, allowing the generator to produce realistic samples for these variables."

title: Synthetic Data Generation with Modified Artificial Bee Colony Optimization Algorithm and Statistical Modeling
summary: This paper proposes a novel synthetic data generation pipeline that uses a modified Artificial Bee Colony optimization algorithm to mimic original data distributions, applies regression-based statistical analysis to assign categorical labels to the generated data, and evaluates the resulting synthetic datasets with supervised machine-learning classifiers across several small real-world datasets. SDV is not run; it is discussed in the related-work section as a prior synthetic data generation system, with the paper noting that SDV's relational modeling approach can produce inaccurate boundaries on noisy parent tables. The Synthetic Data Vault's relational hierarchical modeling concept is only described and critiqued in prose, not executed as part of the proposed method.

title: A Synthetic Data Generation Technique for Enhancement of Prediction Accuracy of Electric Vehicles Demand
summary: This paper forecasts daily rental demand for electric kickboards on Jeju Island by augmenting a small real-world time-series dataset with synthetic data, then feeding the combined data into an ensemble of CatBoost, Random Forest, and XGBoost regressors. The synthetic time-series data are generated using an 'improved CTGAN' model, with a reported hyperparameter table (generator_dim, discriminator_dim, batch_size, generator_lr, discriminator_lr) matching the CTGAN constructor. CTGAN, the conditional tabular GAN from the SDV family, is run as the core data-augmentation generator whose synthetic output the entire empirical forecasting improvement depends on.

CTGAN is cited among the synthetic data generation methods referenced in the surveyed literature, but no SDV component appears to be run or evaluated directly.

title: Using Synthetic Data to Improve the Accuracy of Human Activity Recognition
summary: This conference paper compares three synthetic-data generation techniques for augmenting Human Activity Recognition (HAR) training data derived from the mHealth wearable-sensor dataset, evaluating Decision Tree, Gaussian Naive Bayes, and SVM classifiers on real versus synthetic data. Synthetic Data Vault's Probabilistic Autoregressive model (SDV-PAR) and CTGAN are run directly alongside TimeGAN, with CTGAN at 1500 epochs producing the most realistic and highest-accuracy synthetic dataset. SDV's PAR and CTGAN synthesizers are both run as generators in the empirical comparison, forming the core of the study's results.

title: Synthetic data as meaningful data. On Responsibility in data ecosystems
summary: A philosophical and critical-data-studies paper arguing that synthetic data introduces an analogical, relational perspective on data quality that must be understood through data justice and responsible innovation. It surveys narratives of synthetic data as mirroring or replacing real data across ML fairness, privacy, and public policy discourse, invoking the original SDV paper's claim that synthesized data 'successfully replaced' real data with no measurable difference in downstream use. SDV (Patki et al., 2016) is cited only as an example illustrating claims of synthetic-data fidelity, not run or engaged with technically.

title: Synthetic data in medicine: Legal and ethical considerations for patient profiling
summary: This short communication proposes a legal-ethical framework for evaluating synthetic patient data used in profiling, situating a three-part taxonomy of synthetic data (fully, partially, and hybrid synthetic) within EU regulatory instruments including the GDPR, AI Act, and Medical Devices Regulation. It analyzes profiling practices through the four biomedical ethics principles and calls for governance mechanisms and generation quality benchmarks. The Synthetic Data Vault paper is cited only in a reference list supporting a general claim that synthetic data can closely mirror real datasets, with no engagement with the SDV library or method.
